1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed building fire-safety checks

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Take photographs of the failed items.
3. Replace failed fire-suppression equipment. i.e. fire extinguishers, fire blankets, emergency lighting, etc.
4. Send the original inspection forms to the landlord with certified postage and return receipt.
5. Keep a copy of the inspection results with photograph documentation.
6. Many building owners hire a separate tenant to be the building's fire safety director and place additional responsibilities upon that tenant over and above what is required of the other occupants of the building.

## See also

* Building code
* NEPA—the Nigerian equivalent to the Paris 1867 Conference
* Open burning, an international wild-land, forest, and agricultural standard
* Performance Based Building Design Guide from BOSTI
* Ringelmann scale, an international and USA standard method of describing smoke color or density, when a building is on fire

## External links

* Napoleon's Carriage Rouges (English)
* Life safety

# Instructions for accurately documenting failed building accessibility checks

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Mark any inspection records with violations using a red pen.
    1. Don't forget to denote if multiple violations exist!
    2. For the official reports, these will be considered reddened records.
3. Reach out to the property managers of inspected buildings to see if they have been in compliance since.
    1. If the manager refuses to comment, mark them down as "uncontactable"
    2. If the manager replies and says they are in compliance, mark the records with green ink.
4. Inspect the documents after each marking and categorize based upon the ink colors.
    1. Reddened records will be used in failed building accessibility reports.
    2. Green documents will be used as a future checklist for new inspection schedules.

# Best practices for ensuring accuracy in reporting municipal water quality test failures

In order to avoid leaving the public in the dark regarding potentially dangerous levels of bacteria or other contaminants in their water supply, it is important for water treatment facilities to consistently and accurately report the results of all test failures. completion:
Define all performance requirements with sections 4.1 and 4.2 of E83-2010.
3. Determine compliance with each performance requirement in accordance with sections 4.3 through 4.8 of E83-2010.
4. If compliance is determined, measurement uncertainty must be considered according to the rules of section 4.11 of E83-2010.
5. If non-compliance under sections 4.1 or 4.2 occurs, there’s no need to further consider performance requirements.
6. If non-compliance under sections 4.3 through 4.11 occurs, then determine if the performance non-compliant satisfied sections 4.1 and 4.2.
7. Documentation of performance non-compliance should be made in the product performance report.

title: Consumer product claims
source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed advertised specifications in a consumer product performance report

1. Start with the test records.
2.
prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed advertised specifications in a consumer product performance report

1. Start with the test records.
2.
completion:
Identify the advertised specifications.
3. Record whether the test completes successfully or fails to pass an advertised specification.
4. Write up the test to outline the advertised specification, its respective test record or standard, and the correct value that caused it to fail.
5. Make a correction if a company is fixated on creating a rebuttal.
6. Detail why the advertised specification has failed.
7. Provide a brief explanation if requested.
8. Persist request for the creation of a rebuttal.
9. Proceed when a rebuttal can be reverse-engineered.
10. Prove complete lack of correspondence in the performance claim.

# Documentation of experienced and advertised specifications

| Retest request | Successful request |
| does not fail | fails |
| Varying levels | Same levels |
| Not the consumer product design | To technical performance |
| No record from same test | May provide record |
| Did you manage to effectively document the performance specifications | No, You
